clue.text: Cow-bells used to locate a crafty tie-up?

parts.note: the sound a cow makes
bells ring, so rings are what bells give

explanation.surface: A farmer hangs bells on the cattle to find some cunning knot somewhere in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' is not cunning here but 'to do with craft', i.e. boats, so the tie-up is where a vessel is made fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorings are the ropes, chains and berths by which boats are secured, so they tie up watercraft.

clue.text: Scholars pass round the hat for their wise leader

indicators.note: to pass round something is to go about it, so one piece encircles the other here

parts.note: two Masters of Arts, one MA each side
taken as written; the definite article is surface glue

explanation.surface: Students take up a collection in a hat for the guru who teaches them.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Scholars' means two scholars, each a Master of Arts, and they stand either side like hands passing a hat round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title meaning 'great soul', given to a revered sage, most famously Gandhi.

clue.text: Excursions making inroads into one's income

definitions.meaning: first meaning: trips out, read literally as goings out
second meaning: expenses that eat into what one earns

explanation.surface: Day trips that keep eating into one's wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are expenditure, the money that leaves one's earnings; read literally, they are acts of going out, i.e. excursions.

clue.text: Live and bath in one, perhaps

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters are only one possible arrangement, so they can be set another way

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone lives a simple life and has a bath in one go, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live or dwell in it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Greek debtors on the increase?

definitions.note: a phrase for things that grow; the answer is a noun naming them

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Greek
debtors are those who owe

explanation.surface: A news item about Greece's debtors multiplying.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: growers are things that are getting bigger, on the increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Growers are things that grow, so they are always getting larger in size or number.

clue.text: Sleeping-place given to a girl

parts.note: a bunk on a ship or train
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman is allotted a bunk for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female given name, and crosswords freely use 'girl' to stand for any such name.

clue.text: Executing a.certain Red Queen's orders

parts.note: surface reading: carrying out commands from a Communist leader or a chess queen
setter's reading: the Wonderland queen's constant order is to cut off heads, and 'executing' means putting to death

explanation.surface: Someone dutifully carries out the commands of a revolutionary or a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executing' reads as 'carrying out', but here it means killing; the Lewis Carroll queen's cry is 'Off with their heads!' (strictly the Queen of Hearts).
explanation.definitionFit: Beheading is a form of capital punishment, so it is one way of executing someone.

clue.text: Entreat punishment for the rough stuff

indicators.note: punishment knocks something about, so the word that suffers it is battered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone begs to be punished for some rough behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough stuff' sounds like violence, but 'stuff' is cloth: ratteen is an old coarse woollen fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratteen is a thick, coarse twilled woollen cloth, so it is literally rough material.

clue.text: Inaugural gift of some cash and selected items

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only a portion of the words that follow, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third
surface padding, completing the picture of a gift of goods

explanation.surface: An opening present made up of money and a few chosen things.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsel is a traditional gift marking a beginning, such as a new year, a new venture or a first sale.

clue.text: Incensed with churches taking in cannabis. What a mix-up!

parts.note: hot under the collar, angry

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it within, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church, taken twice for the plural
slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Outrage at churches harbouring cannabis users, followed by an exasperated cry.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'churches' gives two abbreviations, which split to hold the drug. 'Incensed' also hints at church incense, a deliberate distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch is a jumbled mixture, a confused medley, which is exactly a mix-up.

clue.text: Sort of 22 Peg secures

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 22 across is a drink, and this is a deep red Spanish kind of it
second meaning: what a peg holds down

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 22 across leads to WINE; tent is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is a rich red wine from Spain, and a tent is the canvas shelter that pegs fasten to the ground.

clue.text: On which oil might make us row better, lad!

indicators.note: to make something out of material is to form it anew, so these letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowing coach tells a young crewman that some lubricant would improve their stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'to pour oil on troubled waters', meaning to calm a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says oil is poured on troubled waters to soothe them, so they are where oil might be put.

clue.text: Benefice money gives girl a setback

parts.note: a girl's name
taken as written

indicators.note: 'back' tacked onto the word before it tells us to run that word backwards

parts.note: the first three letters of this word, taken as written; the rest is the signal to turn them round

explanation.surface: Church funds deal a blow to some young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' looks like one word meaning a reverse, but it splits into a word plus a direction signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Annates were the first year's revenue of a church benefice, paid by a new incumbent to the Pope.

clue.text: Multiple times the oars men collapse?

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of oarsmen
to fold is to give way or collapse

explanation.surface: A rowing crew keeps collapsing again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Splitting 'oarsmen' into 'oars men' points to the crew rather than individuals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eightfold means eight times as much, a multiple of the original amount.

clue.text: For playing "The music goes round and round"?

definitions.text: For playing "The music goes round and round"?

parts.words: For playing "The music goes round and round"?
parts.note: surface reading: an instrument for performing a particular popular song

parts.words: The music goes round and round
parts.note: setter's reading: an instrument whose music literally goes round, wound on a perforated paper roll

explanation.surface: Something suitable for playing a 1930s novelty song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Music Goes Round and Round' was a popular song; here the round-and-round is the turning paper roll of a player piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a mechanical player piano that plays from a rotating punched paper roll.

clue.text: Begin changing to 18 ac

indicators.note: something that is changing is altering its form, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 18 across

explanation.surface: Instructions to start turning into a figure from legend.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to start or come into being, a straightforward verb synonym for starting.

clue.text: West African theatre makes a loss?

parts.note: abbreviation for West African
the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

explanation.surface: A theatre company in West Africa ends up out of pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastage is the amount lost through waste, leakage or wear, so it is a loss.

clue.text: Like the record up to date

definitions.meaning: first meaning: describing a record, as in the best ever performance
second meaning: covering every period up to the present

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a remark about an old gramophone record still being current.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record is the best ever achieved, and all-time figures cover every moment up to now.

clue.text: Mme Clemenceau?

parts.note: surface reading: the wife of the French statesman
setter's reading: Clemenceau's nickname was 'the Tiger', so his wife would be the female of that animal

explanation.walkthrough: Georges Clemenceau, French prime minister in the First World War, was known as 'le Tigre'.
explanation.definitionFit: If the husband is the Tiger, his wife is the female of that big cat, playfully naming Madame.

clue.text: Arthur's mother had no head for pain

indicators.note: having no head means losing the very first letter of the word in question

parts.note: a severe headache, a type of pain

explanation.surface: King Arthur's mother could not tolerate pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had no head for' sounds like 'could not stand', but it strips the first letter from a headache word, neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend Igraine (Igerna, Ygerne) is the wife of Uther Pendragon and mother of King Arthur.

clue.text: She's in part artless, but has inside information

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an actress whose role, or part, is a naive girl
second, playful meaning: the word begins IN plus GEN, slang for information, so it is 'in on the gen'

explanation.surface: An actress who seems naive on stage actually knows all the secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information; the second half is a joke on the word's spelling rather than a true synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is the stock theatrical role of an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, so she plays an artless part.

clue.text: Intoxicated peer allowed to enter, well tanked up

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other
someone intoxicated is all over the place, so the word described is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A drunken lord is admitted, thoroughly sozzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanked up' suggests drink, matching the surface, but the answer just means full.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity or well fed, so it describes someone thoroughly filled up.

clue.text: Not the sort of potatoes one could get hooked on!

definitions.text: Not the sort of potatoes one could get hooked on!

parts.words: Not the sort of potatoes one could get hooked on!
parts.note: surface reading: some potatoes are too dull to become addicted to
setter's reading: a hook fastens into an eye, and potatoes have eyes, so ones lacking them give a hook nothing to catch

explanation.surface: A joke about potatoes too bland to become addictive.
explanation.walkthrough: The buds on a potato are its eyes; a hook-and-eye fastener needs one, so a potato without them cannot be hooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeless means lacking eyes, describing potatoes with no sprouting buds on their skins.

clue.text: The evening when "Gentlemen, you may smoke"

definitions.text: The evening when "Gentlemen, you may smoke"

parts.words: The evening when "Gentlemen, you may smoke"
parts.note: surface reading: the point at a formal dinner when men are permitted cigars
setter's reading: the official hour at dusk when road vehicles must switch on their lamps

explanation.surface: After the loyal toast at a dinner, the host announces that smoking may begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like the moment to light cigars, but it is the legal time each evening for car headlamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting-up time is the statutory hour after sunset when vehicle lights must be on, so it falls in the evening.

clue.text: Milton's sons of Belial were flown with it

definitions.text: Milton's sons of Belial were flown with it

parts.words: Milton's sons of Belial were flown with it
parts.note: surface reading: devils in Paradise Lost carried by some vehicle
setter's reading: the poem says 'flown with insolence and' a drink, flown meaning flushed or swollen

explanation.walkthrough: Paradise Lost, Book 1: 'the sons of Belial, flown with insolence and wine'. 'Flown' is an old word for flushed, not flying.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation names this drink as what puffed up Belial's riotous followers.

clue.text: Makes "Peso" seem an unusual password

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters are set in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Using a currency name as a secret code looks odd.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Arabian Nights tale of Ali Baba, the magic words open the robbers' cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Open sesame is the magic command from Ali Baba, now any secret phrase or key that gives entry.

clue.text: Well acquainted with metrification?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: skilled or knowledgeable in a subject
second, playful meaning: put into metre, i.e. turned into poetry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Metrification' suggests the 1970s switch to metric units, but here it means setting words to poetic metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Versed means experienced or knowledgeable; it also means rendered into verse, the metrical form of poetry.

clue.text: Hare-brained young things, always in bars

indicators.note: 'in' places one word inside the other, so it sits within the enclosing letters

parts.note: lets are hindrances or obstacles, as in 'without let or hindrance'
ever means always

explanation.surface: Reckless youngsters who are forever propping up pub bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hare-brained' looks like 'foolish', but literally it means having a hare's brain: the definition is young hares.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverets are young hares in their first year, so they are juvenile creatures of the hare kind.
